title: Proof of Delivery Capture and Verification
summary: Check every POD photo or scan for consignment number, date, signature, stamp and remarks, match it to the shipment in your TMS, and flag short, damaged or doubtful deliveries before billing.

seo.title: AI Proof of Delivery (POD) Verification | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that reads POD photos and scans, checks signature, stamp, date and remarks, matches shipments in your TMS and flags exceptions before billing.

problem.intro: For B2B, FTL and PTL shipments, the signed POD or acknowledged lorry receipt copy is what lets you raise an invoice and defend it later. PODs come back as driver phone photos, branch scans or physical copies weeks later, and a billing team checks each one by eye before the shipment can be closed.

pain_points.title: Billing waits for PODs
pain_points.detail: Invoices cannot be raised, or get disputed, until a clean POD is on file, which ties up working capital.

pain_points.title: Unreadable or incomplete PODs
pain_points.detail: Blurred photos, missing consignee stamps, unsigned copies or the wrong LR number surface only when the customer rejects the invoice.

pain_points.title: Remarks missed
pain_points.detail: Handwritten remarks such as short receipt, cartons damaged or seal broken are easy to miss and later become claims nobody prepared for.

pain_points.title: Reused or doubtful PODs
pain_points.detail: The same POD image uploaded against several shipments, or a photo taken far from the delivery address, is hard to spot by hand.

solution.overview: We build a POD verification service that receives images from your driver app, branch scans or email. It reads the LR or AWB number, invoice references, date, package count, consignee name, signature, stamp and handwritten remarks, and matches the POD to the shipment in your TMS. It compares counts with the manifest, picks out remarks that indicate shortage or damage, checks GPS and timestamp metadata against the delivery address where available, and detects reused images. Clean PODs are marked verified for billing; anything incomplete or doubtful goes to an operations reviewer with the reason.
capabilities: Reads LR or AWB number, invoice references, dates, counts and consignee details from photos and scans
Detects signature and consignee stamp, and reads handwritten remarks
Matches each POD to the shipment and invoice in your TMS or ERP
Flags short receipt, damage and refusal remarks for claims and customer follow-up
Checks image location and time against the delivery address where captured
Detects duplicate or reused POD images across shipments

workflow.title: Receive POD images
workflow.detail: PODs arrive from the driver app, branch scanner, WhatsApp, email or customer portal and are queued by shipment.

workflow.title: Extract fields
workflow.detail: The system reads shipment number, dates, counts, consignee details, signature, stamp and remarks.

workflow.title: Match to shipment
workflow.detail: Extracted values are matched to the TMS record and manifest, including package counts.

workflow.title: Run checks
workflow.detail: Completeness, remark, duplicate-image and location checks run on each POD.

workflow.title: Review exceptions
workflow.detail: Incomplete, mismatched or doubtful PODs go to an operations reviewer, who accepts, rejects or requests a re-upload.

workflow.title: Release for billing
workflow.detail: Verified PODs are marked in the TMS, attached to the invoice and published to the customer portal.

human_in_the_loop: Operations reviewers decide every incomplete, mismatched or doubtful POD and request re-uploads from drivers or branches. Shortage and damage claims are raised and settled by your claims team, not by the system.
integrations: TMS such as an in-house system, Oracle OTM or SAP TM
WhatsApp Business API, email and shared drives for branch uploads
guardrails: Low-confidence fields always reviewed before a POD is verified
Duplicate and location checks flag, never auto-reject
Original images retained unaltered with an audit log
Consignee personal data masked in logs and access-restricted
compliance_notes: Consignee details and photos are personal data under the DPDP Act 2023; retention follows your contractual and tax record requirements.
A verified POD record with audit trail helps you evidence delivery in customer disputes and tax audits.

pilot.scope: PODs from one region or one key account, using recent PODs already checked by your billing team, plus a live parallel run.

what_we_measure.how: Extracted shipment numbers, dates and counts compared with billing team records.
Flagged PODs that reviewers confirm as genuinely incomplete, mismatched or doubtful.
Shortage and damage remarks found by reviewers compared with those the system flagged.
Time from POD upload to invoice-ready status, with and without the pipeline.

faqs.q: Our drivers send PODs on WhatsApp. Can you work with that?
faqs.a: Yes. A WhatsApp Business number can receive POD photos and link them to the shipment by LR number or driver mapping. Many operators move to an app later, but WhatsApp is a quick start.

faqs.q: Can it read handwritten remarks in Hindi?
faqs.a: Handwritten remarks in English and Hindi are read and classified, and anything the system is unsure of goes to review. The pilot reports remark accuracy separately.
No. It marks PODs as verified or sends them to a reviewer with the reason. Rejections and re-upload requests are decided by your operations team.

faqs.q: Does this work for e-commerce ePODs with OTP?
faqs.a: Yes. The same checks apply to photo or OTP-based ePODs, with more weight on location, time and duplicate checks than on signatures.
